sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Compiler settings for the mobile app
sections.what: Sets how TypeScript checks the mobile app. It inherits a shared base, adds a shorthand for the source folder, and lists every TypeScript file in the app as part of the project.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps mobile settings consistent with other apps by reusing one shared base. Reason for the shorthand is not stated.
sections.watch_out: The shorthand only works if the bundler and the editor use the same mapping, so changing one without the other causes import errors.

summary: Sets the TypeScript compiler rules for the mobile app, including a short import prefix that points to the source folder.
purpose: Lets the mobile app's code use short import paths and tells the compiler which files belong to the app.
why: Likely reason: reuses a shared React Native base configuration from the workspace and adds only the import shortcut and file list. Reason for the shortcut is not stated.
how: First the file inherits the shared React Native base rules. Then it maps the at-sign prefix to the source folder. Last it says that every TypeScript and TSX file under the app folder is part of the project.
inputs: The shared base configuration in the workspace package, and the app's source files.
outputs: Compiler settings used when the app is type checked or built.
risks: The include list covers every file under the app, so generated or temporary files there may also be checked. A missing base package breaks every build.
debug: If imports with the at-sign prefix fail, check that the bundler also knows this mapping. If type checks fail after a base change, compare the shared base file. Run the app's typecheck command if one exists.
